item.title: Yamaha to skip Qatar Grand Prix over security concerns
item.description:
Yamaha to skip Qatar Grand Prix over security concerns

Yamaha will not participate in the Qatar Grand Prix of MotoGP, after concerns over the country's security situation.

In a statement, MotoGP said it was disappointed by Yamaha's decision, but noted that the company decided to not change its "company-wide travel restrictions." 

"MotoGP is disappointed by Yamaha's decision not to participate in the Qatar Grand Prix. While we recognise the team is subject to a broader corporate policy restricting travel to the Middle East, we do not believe this decision reflects the extensive assurances provided to all championship stakeholders," said MotoGP in a statement.

"Following consultation with the State of Qatar, Lusail International Circuit, independent safety advisers and MotoGP's own ongoing risk assessment process, MotoGP has not received any information that would warrant a change to the current plans for the event."

item.title: Israeli army builds new roads linking military posts in southern Lebanon
item.description: The Israeli army is building new roads through mountains and valleys in southern Lebanon to connect its military positions, Lebanon’s National News Agency (NNA) reported Saturday, Anadolu reports. The work spans the western and central sectors of southern Lebanon, where Israeli forces have established military posts on occupied Lebanese territory, according to the agency. NNA said the construction was taking place alongside Israeli demolition operations in the area. The central sector includes the towns of Aita al-Shaab, Maroun al-Ras, Bint Jbeil and Aitaroun. Maroun al-Ras overlooks the Israeli settlement of Avivim across the border. item.title: ‘People are dying in so many ways’: Tent fire kills 2 infant girls in Gaza
item.description: Habiba was due for her two-month vaccinations on Saturday. Instead, her family mourned her death alongside that of seven-month-old Aseel after a fire tore through the tent where their relatives had gathered in the southern Gaza Strip, Anadolu reports. The family’s visit in al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis, ended in a desperate attempt to save the two infants when flames broke out Friday afternoon. Both suffered severe burns and were admitted to intensive care. They died Saturday morning. Nasser Medical Complex identified them as Habiba Mohammed Zanoun, two months old, and Aseel Abu Suhayban, seven months old. Sources told Anadolu that the fire started while food was being cooked inside the tent. Severe shortages of cooking gas and basic supplies […]

item.title: Iran has 'no intention' to engage in peace talks with US as war looms
item.description:
Iran has 'no intention' to engage in peace talks with US as war looms

Submitted by MEE staff on Sun, 11/01/2026 - 11:00
Tehran dismisses diplomatic breakthrough with Washington as war of words escalates, while Rubio claims Trump has not made a decision on restarting war on Iran
A man walking past a mural showing Iran's leadership in Tehran (AFP)
Off

Iran said it has “no intention” of engaging in talks with the United States, as the war of words between the two countries intensifies.

During a parliamentary session, Ali Nikzad, deputy speaker of Iran’s parliament, claimed the US had “nothing new to offer” in potential talks.

“They must accept that they have no choice but to acknowledge the power of Iran,” said Nikzad. “It is the Americans, not the Iranian nation, who will ultimately surrender in this conflict. [Tehran] has no intention of negotiating on the nuclear issue regardless of any pressure."

The deputy speaker said that “this great nation has already granted its enemies ample opportunity for negotiations in this arena, but it was met only with repeated breaches of promises and the illegal bombardment of parts of its peaceful nuclear facilities”.

Nikzad’s intervention comes after the Iranian army vowed to respond to any new US attacks with “an immediate, crushing response”.

Earlier on Sunday, the Iranian army's spokesperson, Mohammad Akraminia, stressed that Iran’s war strategy has shifted from a “purely defensive stance to an offensive approach some time ago".

“Should a new war erupt, the geography of the conflict will not be confined to the West Asia region,” Akraminia told Iran state media. “Any potential future war could prove significantly longer than past conflicts.” 

US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that the United States has knocked out much of Iran’s military but still had to "take care of" one or two targets.

'Escalation is coming': Middle East on edge as new Israeli-US attack on Iran looms
Read More »

"We've knocked out their nuclear. We still have to take care of, I would say, one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes," Trump said.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, however, said Trump has not made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran, and that the US would be open to a diplomatic solution.

The United Arab Emirates, meanwhile, said it hoped for a breakthrough between Iran and the US while preparing for the worst.

"We're hoping that there is a diplomatic breakthrough," diplomatic adviser to the Emirati president Anwar Gargash said during a conference in Manama.

"It is not the interest of the region to go through another round... But I think we're also, as we've shown before, braced for the worst."

Following a visit to Tehran this week by a Qatari delegation, Iran has dispatched envoys to the Gulf country to continue consultations as part of indirect negotiations with the US to end the war.

US warns Gulf of intense strikes on Iran after midterms: Report
Read More »

Earlier this week, US Senator Chris Murphy described Trump's plan to restart the war on Iran as "insane" and said it would lead to a "devastating escalation".

"You've heard a preview that it would be a short-duration plan. I'll just say this: their plan is insane," Murphy said, speaking at an event organised by the Middle East Institute in Washington, DC.

"It will lead to devastating escalation and the likely destruction of our commitment to the rule of law."

Murphy, a member of the Senate Foreign Relations and Appropriations committees, made the comments after American media reported that the US warned several Gulf Arab countries to be prepared for a short, intense military offensive against Iran after the US midterm elections on 3 November.

The war began on 28 February with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran. Iran retaliated by targeting, among others, Gulf countries hosting US military bases.

Araghchi says Hormuz could be reopened within two days if conditions met
item.description:
Araghchi says Hormuz could be reopened within two days if conditions met

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said Hormuz could be reopened within two days if Washington agrees to a set of conditions, including the formal recognition of the new shipping route designated by Iran and Oman in the Strait of Hormuz.

In an interview with Al Jazeera, Araghchi said other conditions include lifting the sanctions the US imposed on Iran after the collapse of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding (MoU) in July; reducing the US military presence in the region; reinstating the oil waivers granted in June as part of the MoU; releasing frozen Iranian funds, including those held in Qatar; formally recognising the new shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz, set by Iran and Oman, and closing all other routes and ending the war on all fronts, particularly Israel’s attacks on Lebanon.

Araghchi told Al Jazeera that the plan currently under discussion is the one Iran originally presented at the beginning, known as the Iran seven-day plan, in which "we specified our condition for reopening the Strait of Hormuz".

"Our Qatari friends asked to cut this time window from seven days to five days or less, and we worked on this idea during the Qatari delegation visit yesterday,” he said.

“We have now reached a plan that cuts the implementation time to two days. On day one, the US implements a set of measures. On day two, the Hormuz Strait will reopen, and navigation will be restored to what it used to be.”

item.title: Israeli, American flags burnt during protest in France
item.description:
Israeli, American flags burnt during protest in France

Israeli and American flags were burned during a cost-of-living protest in Lyon, France. 

Footage shared by Clash Report shows protesters stomping Israeli and American flags on the roof of the Jean-Macé tram shelter in Lyon before setting them on fire.

Nearby protesters were heard chanting “Israel assassin".
